newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end higher, buoyed by overseas fund.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end higher, buoyed by overseas fund.

text.p: China's B shares for foreign investors closed higher on Friday, ending the week on a positive note as funds flowed back into the market from abroad, brokers said.
Hot money from Hong Kong was seen returning to the local bourse after that market's recent surge, they said.

The Shanghai B share index put on 0.887 point or 1.22 percent to 73.790 on volume of 9.242 million shares compared with 10.321 million shares on Thursday. Shenzhen's B share index rose 1.25 points or 0.97 percent to 130.86.
"Some of the hot money has begun to flow back to the B share market as the upward potential for H shares in Hong Kong may be limited after the recent gains," one broker said.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index touched another record high on Friday but profit-taking slowed its advance.

Demand on China's major market was focused on Shanghai Chlor-Alkali Chemical, which was the latest company to benefit from talk of a restructuring. Its shares rose $0.008 or 3.39 percent to $0.244 on volume of 822,500 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance was also in favour as it gained $0.036 or 2.91 percent to $1.270.
Dazhong Taxi was up $0.014 to $0.834 after it reported a 52.7 percent rise in first-half profits. It linked the rise to an expanded taxi and bus fleet.
On the Shenzhen bourse, the big gainer was Bengang Steel, which reversed recent losses to climb HK$0.06 to HK$2.07.
On the markets for domestic investors, Shanghai's A share index finished a modest 2.897 points higher at 1,248.475 while Shenzhen's A share index gained 1.96 point to 409.46.
